text:
The Federal Aviation Administration issued certification for the Boeing 737 MAX-10, a critical milestone that enables the aircraft to enter commercial service and expands the manufacturer’s narrow-body fleet capabilities [FAA issued the certification](https://www.faa.gov/newsroom/federal-aviation-administration-issues-certification-boeing-737-max-10). This action coincides with the agency adopting a new airworthiness directive for certain Boeing 737-600 through -900ER series airplanes, highlighting ongoing regulatory oversight of the manufacturer’s safety compliance [FAA adopted the directive](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/10/19/2026-21332/airworthiness-directives-the-boeing-company-airplanes). The Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration also finalized a decision to renew and modify an exemption for the Association of American Railroads and the American Short Line and Regional Railroad Association regarding hours of service, adjusting operational flexibility for rail carriers [FMCSA finalized the decision](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/10/21/2026-21488/hours-of-service-of-drivers-association-of-american-railroads-and-american-short-line-and-regional).

U.S. Transportation Secretary Sean P. Duffy announced the first-ever Special Airworthiness Market Survey Certificate for electric vertical takeoff and landing aircraft, establishing a new regulatory pathway for advanced air mobility developers to conduct market surveys before full certification [Secretary Duffy announced the certificate](https://www.faa.gov/newsroom/trumps-transportation-secretary-sean-p-duffy-announces-first-ever-special-airworthiness). The Secretary also announced New Mexico’s first demonstration flight under the Electric Vertical Takeoff and Landing Integration Pilot Program, signaling progress in integrating these vehicles into the national airspace system [Secretary Duffy announced the flight](https://www.faa.gov/newsroom/trumps-transportation-secretary-sean-p-duffy-announces-new-mexicos-first-advanced-air). These developments reflect a broader trend of the Federal Aviation Administration creating specific frameworks to manage emerging aviation technologies while maintaining safety standards.

The Federal Aviation Administration imposed a ban on unauthorized drones along the U.S.-Mexico border through 2027 to counter cartel threats, significantly restricting unmanned aircraft operations in that airspace [FAA imposed the ban](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiYkFVX3lxTE0yT2J0U1AwMVB3Z3JUcDN3WmE0ZXBCQmFaNHMwNlpSVExrQjg4MmsteTg1dC10c0xKXzh1a1RXdE5TRlkwcEhNZ2FZRGR6Q2JIWS1hOW01N0QzaFBDWmpUV1h3). This security measure aligns with the Department of Defense marking one year of accelerating counter-unmanned aircraft systems capabilities through Joint Interagency Task Force 401, demonstrating coordinated efforts to enhance airspace security [DoD marked the anniversary](https://www.war.gov/News/News-Stories/Article/Article/4626931/joint-interagency-task-force-401-marks-one-year-of-accelerating-counter-uas-cap/). Additionally, Echodyne and ACS signed a strategic collaboration agreement to advance counter-drone capabilities worldwide, indicating increased private sector investment in defense technologies [Echodyne and ACS signed the agreement](https://news.google.).

In autonomous vehicle developments, the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration opened a probe into Tesla robotaxis for alleged speeding and ignoring school zones, intensifying regulatory scrutiny on self-driving deployments [NHTSA opened the probe](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMic0FVX3lxTE8zQThsSmRPZXVoOHRjRmt6QllXU1lQYkJuQ0o1ckdVX2lDbmg0Nk4yTnlyamxqU0lnanc2Qk1sdVJZMlFRUE1BN1lwSFZiVzl3U2NBWFBWN1I5VDA4cEZFUHBEdkNYb1JhLS0xbmtCNlduQ1E). Despite this investigation, latest data showed Tesla Cybercabs recorded no major incidents, presenting a complex picture of safety performance versus operational compliance [Tesla recorded no major incidents](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiggFBVV95cUxNQUxDN1pTU2pteUZaVTcxR3BRN3QxOExzdGVtYl9CYzFwbDZlSkRva0FnYlk1ek1DVzYtbFhCMlJNdWFFcTFYVHA2cklXdDNzZHl5dGYtVGg3RjZDY3NfWEw5bEdIQ1NEVTRxR1BZenpSaTRtWm5oa3Yxd1hTRzVEVUdB). The Federal Aviation Administration also proposed a $351,000 civil penalty against Creamer Pilot Services for alleged unauthorized passenger-carrying operations, reinforcing enforcement actions against regulatory violations in general aviation [FAA proposed the penalty](https://www.faa.gov/newsroom/faa-proposes-351000-fine-against-creamer-pilot-services-alleged-unauthorized-passenger).
